correctness.rationale: A q-colored nonempty chain of K nested equivalences is uniquely an unordered hierarchy of height K+1; root automorphism group is product over child-types of Aut(U) wreath S_m. Order exactly 1 iff all children are rigid with multiplicity 0 or1, and exactly2 iff either one unique order-two child plus a set of rigid children or one rigid type duplicated exactly twice plus the others distinct. These disjoint cases imply R_(h+1)=F_h-1 and T_(h+1)=F_h T_h +F_h sum_s R_[z^s] z^(2s)/(1+z^s). Derivative at z=1 gives C_h, maximal-degree comparison yields B_h=1+sum C_i and exactly q top C2 types, while contiguous subset-sum induction realizes every size 1..C and 2..B. Independent fresh exact polynomial multiplication for q=2,K=1 yields R2=2z+2z^2+2z^3+z^4; T2=4z^2+8z^3+11z^4+12z^5+7z^6+2z^7, matching all coefficients. The general theorem rests on the wreath and subset-sum proof, not finite enumeration.

originality.rationale: Fiuk 2026 provides the same nested-equivalence semantic object and hierarchy representation for guarded finite-model theory. Imrich--Tucker rooted asymmetrizing-color arguments provide the distinct-branch rigidity principle. Neither inspected result gives coupled rigid/C2 generating functions, exact one-involution upper capacity, or all intermediate sizes. A 2012 Sparsity monograph lemma potentially bounds existence of involutions, full implications not inspected.
residual_risks: Sparsity 2012 Lemma 6.10 or an older bounded-height colored-tree automorphism enumerator may subsume capacity or coupled recurrences.
The finite polynomial check covers q=2,K=1 only; general no-gap spectrum proved by subset-sum induction, not computation.
Full classification concerns exactly two automorphisms; it does not classify higher automorphism-group orders.
